decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

The proposed development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the materials detailed under page 5 of the application form and approved plans unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the proposed development will harmonise with the character of the surrounding area.

Statement Required by Article 35(2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management) Order 2015: No significant problems were identified during the consideration of the application, and therefore it has been determined in accordance with paragraph 38 of the National Planning Policy Framework.
description:
I am requesting two elements for planning approval 

1. The development proposes to remove the existing, damaged sandstone paving and pointing and replace it with new cobble paving, whilst also changing the design slightly to allow better access for the parking of cars and will avoid cars damaging the edge of the turf which is unavoidable with the current design. This will require changing from a curved edge to a straight edge and reducing the grassed area by a small amount. There will still remain a sizeable area of turf, flower beds and hedging not dissimilar to the current look.  
The front and side hedges will be retained and not changed 
Flower bed will be the same and a magnolia tree will also be retained in the centre of the lawn 
Large soakaway drain already in place under the lawned area to receive rainwater 

2. I wish to replace the existing UPVC white windows which are over 30 years old and no longer efficient. The windows are to be a direct replacement of the existing white UPVC windows, however I wish to enhance the look to be more in keeping with the area by having a white UPVC woodgrain affect included as well as external astragal bars to give the look of wooden windows. The attached neighbouring house also has UPVC white windows (changed 2 years ago) so would be in keeping with the road. 

The windows to be replaced are four front windows and two side windows to the ground floor and one side window to the first floor bathroom 

The works will be in keeping with the road and houses within it. I am looking to enhance the property in line with the conservation area principles
